name: SC-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 13 points and Clyburn is a decades-entrenched incumbent
Clyburn holds a roughly $1.9 million cash advantage against a challenger with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent
No public polling or expert ratings flag any competitiveness
model.rationale: A D+13 district, an incumbent of Clyburn's stature and name recognition, and a lopsided money edge leave no realistic path for the Republican challenger; markets and fundamentals point the same way. With no polls or rating movement suggesting otherwise, the seat stays firmly Safe D.
model.watch: Only news of diminished incumbent activity, a health or ethics surprise, or unexpected challenger-funded polling would justify revisiting this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 6th District, anchored in Columbia and stretching through the rural Lowcountry, leans Democratic by roughly thirteen points. Jim Clyburn, the longtime incumbent and former House Majority Whip, seeks another term with about $1.9 million in the bank, while Republican John Peterson shows no reported fundraising. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the contest. Prediction markets put Clyburn's chances near 96 percent.

The combination of a strongly Democratic seat, an incumbent with exceptional name recognition, and a large financial gap makes an upset hard to construct. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves room around the expected margin, though Clyburn has historically won by wide double-digit margins. The district remains solidly Democratic heading into November.
